description: Figure 1 (right) is a small line plot illustrating a loss comparison between two methods (“Vanilla” and “SepLLM”) as a function of computation cost. The x-axis is labeled “TFLOPs” on a linear scale, spanning approximately 0 to 1.25 with regularly spaced tick labels at about 0.25 intervals (0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00, 1.25). The y-axis is labeled “Loss” on a linear scale, ranging roughly from 2.45 up to about 2.75 with tick labels at about 0.05 intervals (e.g., 2.45, 2.50, 2.55, 2.60, 2.65, 2.70, 2.75). Two solid lines are shown: a blue line labeled “Vanilla” and a red line labeled “SepLLM,” with no visible point markers. Both lines decrease as TFLOPs increases; the blue Vanilla curve starts near the top of the axis around loss ≈2.75 at very low TFLOPs and declines to about ≈2.52 by TFLOPs ≈1.25, while the red SepLLM curve starts slightly below the blue near ≈2.74 at very low TFLOPs and declines to about ≈2.50 by TFLOPs ≈1.25. A green dashed horizontal reference line is drawn at approximately loss = 2.55, annotated “1.28×” near the right side of the plot.
